title: Exact Minimax Gap for the Coordinate Sign Family
summary: Establishes the exact relationship between a fixed query budget T and error LR(1−√(T/d)).
use_when: Establishes the exact relationship between a fixed query budget T and error LR(1−√(T/d)).

statement.objects_and_definitions: Q=B_2(R)⊂R^d; f_v=(L/√d)〈v,x〉, v∈{±1}^d. Loss: f_v(xhat)−min_Q f_v.
assumptions: Only the coordinate-gradient oracle is available: query(i,x)→Lv_i/√d; no function values or full gradients.
d,L,R and the function family are public; v is unknown.
All adaptive randomized algorithms, arbitrary feasible outputs; at most T calls on every execution path; free internal computation.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: inf_A sup_{v∈{±1}^d} E_A[gap_A(v)]; v is fixed independently of algorithmic randomness. The uniform sign prior is used only to prove the lower bound.

complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper bound: alg.coordinate_sign_recovery; the lower bound covers all adaptive randomized algorithms described above.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: xhat∈B_2(R); function gap; take expectation over algorithmic randomness first, then the supremum over fixed instances.
complexity_scope.guarantee: Expected error for each fixed v; the call budget is a deterministic upper bound on every execution path.

map: Uniform sign prior and conditional independence
Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the contribution of known coordinates
From an average over instances to the existence of a fixed instance
Recovery on fixed coordinates attains the lower bound
proofs.full_local_argument:
First, ||∇f_v||_2=L, the optimizer is x_v^*=-R v/sqrt(d), and the optimal value is -LR.
Upper bound: if T=0, output 0. If T>=1, query a fixed set S of T distinct coordinates and output
x_i=-R v_i/sqrt(T) (i∈S), with all other coordinates 0. The norm is R and the function value is -LR sqrt(T/d),
so the stated gap holds for every v. No randomness is used.

Lower bound: first let v have independent uniform signs, with the algorithm's random seed independent of v. After fixing the seed,
a transcript fixes only the signs of coordinates already queried. The next coordinate and query point are chosen adaptively from the existing
transcript; unqueried signs remain conditionally independent with mean 0. This follows inductively: querying a known
coordinate adds no constraint, while querying a new coordinate fixes only that sign. Let S be the final set of distinct queried coordinates;
then |S|<=T. Conditional on the transcript and seed, the output xhat is a known vector in Q, so
E[f_v(xhat)|history,seed]=(L/sqrt(d)) sum_{i∈S}v_i xhat_i
>=-(L/sqrt(d))*sqrt(|S|)*||xhat_S||_2>=-LR sqrt(T/d).
Thus the average gap over random v and the algorithm's seed is >=LR(1-sqrt(T/d)). Since the set of v is finite, there exists
a fixed v whose expected gap over algorithmic randomness alone is at least this value. Combining with the upper bound yields equality.
proofs.omitted_details: None; assumptions are expanded in the statement.

title: Fixed-Coordinate Recovery Algorithm
summary: Provides a simple upper-bound witness attaining the exact minimax gap for the linear sign family.
use_when: Provides a simple upper-bound witness attaining the exact minimax gap for the linear sign family.

variants.name: Fixed Set of T Coordinates
public_inputs: The function belongs to the publicly known sign family
variants.state_and_initialization: S={1,...,T}; make no queries when T=0.
variants.requirements: Linear sign family and an exact coordinate-gradient oracle; Q=B_2(R).
variants.query_and_update: Query i∈S sequentially and recover v_i=√d·∂_i f/L. For T>0, set x_i=−Rv_i/√T(i∈S) and all other coordinates to 0.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Exactly T calls, with no additional stopping information.
variants.output: Output 0 if T=0; otherwise output the x∈Q defined above.
variants.cost: T coordinate calls; storage of T signs.

components.name: Euclidean Normalization of Known Coordinates
components.goal: Maximize the contribution of known coordinates to the linear objective within the budget.
components.operation: Scale the recovered sign vector in the negative direction to radius R.
components.requires: Euclidean ball; linear objective; known coordinate gradients.
components.cost_effect: O(T) internal computation; no additional oracle calls.
transfer_checks: No longer valid for nonlinear objectives.
Other norms require optimization using the corresponding dual norm.

title: From Full-Space Function Gap to Gradient Norm
summary: Converts the function gap to squared gradient norm under global L-smoothness and a finite global infimum.
use_when: Converts the function gap to squared gradient norm under global L-smoothness and a finite global infimum.

statement.objects_and_definitions: f:R^d→R is C^1; Euclidean norm; f_*=inf_{R^d} f.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: Holds pointwise for every x∈R^d; no randomness.

proofs.full_local_argument: Set y=x−∇f(x)/L. L-smoothness gives f(y)≤f(x)+〈∇f(x),y−x〉+(L/2)||y−x||²=f(x)−||∇f(x)||²/(2L). Using f_*≤f(y) and rearranging yields the conclusion.
proofs.omitted_details: The descent inequality follows directly by integrating the Lipschitz condition along a line segment.

sensitive_conditions: Not requiring convexity does not exclude convexity
